readingInstruction: Read Matthew 17:1-18:35. Jesus is transfigured on the mountain, the Father speaks, and then Jesus teaches about greatness, discipline, and forgiveness. Read the Transfiguration in light of the end of chapter 16.
settingTheScene: Six days after Peter’s confession and Jesus’ first prediction of his death, Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain. There his appearance changes, and Moses and Elijah, the law and the prophets, appear and speak with him. It is a glimpse of his glory, given to strengthen the disciples for the road to the cross. Then, in chapter 18, Jesus gives teaching on life in the community of the kingdom.
observation: “And he was transfigured before them, and his face shone like the sun, and his clothes became white as light” (17:2).
“And behold, there appeared to them Moses and Elijah, talking with him” (17:3).
“This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased; listen to him” (17:5).
“Jesus came and touched them, saying, Rise, and have no fear” (17:7).
“If you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, Move from here to there, and it will move” (17:20).
“Unless you turn and become like children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven” (18:3).
“For where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I among them” (18:20).
“I do not say to you seven times, but seventy-seven times” (18:22).
interpretation:
On the mountain, the disciples see the glory that is usually hidden. Jesus shines like the sun, and Moses and Elijah, who both met God on a mountain, speak with him. Luke tells us they spoke of his “departure,” literally his exodus, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem. The law and the prophets bear witness to Jesus and his coming death.

Peter wants to build three tents, but a cloud covers them, and the Father says almost the same words as at the baptism, with an addition: “Listen to him.” Moses and Elijah fade away. Jesus alone remains. The Law and the Prophets point to him, and now the voice of heaven says that he is the one to hear. When they look up, they see only Jesus.

Coming down, they find the disciples failing to heal a boy, and Jesus tells them that even a small faith moves mountains. He again predicts his death and resurrection.

In chapter 18, Jesus teaches that greatness in the kingdom belongs to the humble like children. He warns about causing little ones to stumble and tells the story of the lost sheep: the Father does not want any to perish. He then gives a process for restoring a sinning brother, and promises his presence where two or three gather in his name.

Peter asks how often to forgive, and Jesus says seventy-seven times. The parable of the unforgiving servant follows, a man forgiven a huge debt who refuses to forgive a small one. The lesson is that those who have been forgiven much must forgive. The mercy we have received is the pattern and power for the mercy we give.
connection: Exodus 34:29-35 shows Moses’ face shining. 2 Peter 1:16-18 recalls Peter’s witness of this event. Luke 9:31 mentions the exodus Jesus would accomplish. Deuteronomy 18:15 promises a prophet like Moses to whom Israel should listen. Hebrews 1:1-2 says God has spoken to us by his Son. Colossians 3:13: “As the Lord has forgiven you, so you also must forgive.” Ephesians 4:32. Revelation 1:12-18.
application:
Listen to Jesus this week. Read a Gospel passage slowly, with the sense that the Father is saying, “Listen to him.”

Think of someone who has wronged you. Consider the size of your own forgiven debt, and take a step toward forgiveness.

Seek out a small child or a humble person and learn something about trust.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to help you listen to his beloved Son.
Thank him for showing his glory to strengthen you.
Ask him to make you someone who forgives.
